patients.label: 10-year-old castrated male Maltese dog with cranial cruciate ligament rupture and mitral valve disease treated with combined intra- and extracapsular stabilization

identity_evidence.quote: A 10-year-old castrated male Maltese, weighing 2.0 kg, was referred

attribution_limitations: The case text says the previous TTT site rendered osteotomy-based stabilization unsuitable and the abstract says osteotomy was contraindicated; these are author judgments, not recorded as a declined or cancelled procedure.

The Figure 1 caption calls the radiographs postoperative images from the previous patella surgery, yet panel B is described as revealing CDM indicating CrCL rupture, which the text places at the current presentation.

The discussion says the approach avoided the use of implants and notes the absence of hardware, while the case text and Figure 2 caption describe a synthetic ligament, a clamp system and a stainless-steel crimp. The discussion contrasts the technique with osteotomy fixation hardware and preserved bone architecture and never names the ligament, clamp or crimp, so it is not treated as a same-item conflict; no implant-free fact is recorded.

The anchor of "After 1 month" for the start of leash walking is not stated; the preceding sentence gives about 4 weeks of cage rest after bandage removal, and the discussion says complete functional recovery within 4 weeks.

The furosemide sentence says its natriuretic and kaliuretic effects warranted periodic electrolyte monitoring for potential hypokalemia; it is a drug-level statement and does not state that monitoring was done or that hypokalemia occurred.
The Figure 2 caption names a polyethylene filament line in the 3D bone models; the text does not state the material of the Ligafiba synthetic ligament.

evidence.quote: Ventrodorsal view showing prior TTT fixation.
Lateral view revealing CDM, indicating CrCL rupture.
(A) Ruptured cranial cruciate ligament (blue circle) observed within the stifle joint.
(B) Appearance of the joint after debridement of the ruptured ligament (blue circle).
(C) Final placement of the intra-articular prosthetic ligament, mimicking the anatomical position of the native CrCL (blue circle).
(D) Ventrodorsal view demonstrating lateral crimp fixation of the prosthetic ligament.
(E) Lateral view confirming elimination of CDM and appropriate tibial alignment without displacement.
(F) Frontal view showing the intra-articular ligament passing from the distal lateral femur to the medial tibia.
(G) Lateral view showing the extracapsular extension and fixation on the lateral aspect of the tibia, resembling conventional suture anchor techniques.

claims.text: A 10-year-old castrated male Maltese weighing 2.0 kg was referred for acute non-weight-bearing right hind limb lameness. History included bilateral tibial tuberosity transposition one year earlier for medial patellar luxation, stage B2 myxomatous mitral valve disease, and pimobendan, furosemide and enalapril.

evidence.quote: A 10-year-old castrated male Maltese
acute, non-weight-bearing lameness in the right hind limb
weighing 2.0 kg
One year prior, the patient had undergone bilateral tibial tuberosity transposition (TTT) for correction of medial patellar luxation.
Medical history also included stage B2 myxomatous mitral valve disease managed.
The patient was receiving pimobendan (Vetmedin^(®), Boehringer Ingelheim, Germany; 0.25 mg/kg PO BID)

Furosemide (Lasix^(®), Handok Pharmaceutical, Korea; 0.5 mg/kg PO BID), a loop diuretic acting on the Na^(+)–K^(+)−2Cl^(−) symporter of the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle, was used to relieve pulmonary congestion.
Enalapril (Enap^(®), Donga ST, Korea; 0.5 mg/kg PO BID), an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor, was given to reduce afterload and suppress renin-angiotensin activation.

claims.text: Examination showed a positive cranial drawer motion of the right stifle, and radiographs confirmed cranial displacement of the tibia with mild periarticular osteophyte formation, consistent with cranial cruciate ligament rupture. Prior TTT changes were noted, and pre-anesthetic screening revealed no contraindications to anesthesia.

claims.text: Under butorphanol and midazolam premedication, propofol induction and sevoflurane maintenance, with bupivacaine infiltration, a hybrid intra-articular and extracapsular stabilization was performed using 1.1-mm bone tunnels and a Ligafiba synthetic ligament with clamp, bypassing the lateral fabella. A Robert Jones bandage was applied for 7 days, followed by strict cage rest for about 4 weeks.
